## How to evaluate HOA management companies in Chicago.
Most boards compare proposals on the monthly fee alone, and most regret it within a year. These are the six questions we would ask any firm, including us, before signing.

### Total annual cost, not the headline fee
Compare the full year: base management fee, per-item charges for mailings and violation letters, transition fees, and any percentage taken on capital projects. CenterPoint quotes one flat monthly fee, no percentage-of-budget pricing and no separate capital-project oversight fee.

### Who actually manages your community
Ask how many communities your assigned manager carries and how often that assignment changes. Every CenterPoint community works with one dedicated manager who attends your meetings, walks your property, and answers a direct line.

### Financial reporting you can audit
A board should see monthly statements with every invoice attached, not a quarterly summary. Ask each candidate firm for a sample report package and the date it typically arrives each month.

### Enforcement with due process
Consistent, documented CC&R enforcement protects property values and protects the board from claims of selective treatment. Ask how violations are logged, noticed, escalated, and reported back to the board.

### What happens after 5 PM
Storm damage, water intrusion, and access failures do not schedule themselves inside business hours. Confirm whether the emergency line is answered by the firm’s own local staff or routed to a national call center.

### Exit terms before entry terms
Read the termination clause before signing: notice period, early-exit penalties, and who owns your records. A firm confident in its service does not need to lock boards in.

## Switching HOA managers, without the chaos.
Boards stay with underperforming firms because the handover feels risky. Here is exactly what the first ninety days look like when a community moves to CenterPoint, your board signs, and we carry the rest.

### Weeks 1-2 · Records & access
We issue the records request to your outgoing firm, collect governing documents, contracts, owner ledgers, and keys, and stand up your association in our systems.

### Weeks 3-6 · Money & vendors
Bank accounts transfer under board control, assessment collection is redirected, vendors are notified and re-papered, and owners receive a welcome letter with portal credentials.

### Weeks 7-12 · The new standard
Your dedicated manager walks the property, builds the maintenance calendar, reviews the budget and reserves with the board, and delivers the first full monthly report package.

## What HOA boards should ask a prospective manager.
Clear scope, clear pricing, and a transition plan your board can evaluate before making a decision.

### What does an HOA management company actually do?
Day to day: assessment collection and accounting, monthly financial reporting with invoices attached, vendor bidding and supervision for landscaping, snow removal, and common-area maintenance, fair CC&R enforcement with documented due process, board meeting preparation and minutes, owner communications and portal support, and a 24/7 emergency line. The board keeps every decision; the manager executes them and reports back.

### How is HOA management different from rental property management?
An HOA manager works for the association and carries out board-approved community operations. A rental manager works for landlords and tenants. CenterPoint serves community associations only and does not manage rental apartments.

### How much does HOA management cost in Chicago?
CenterPoint HOA management starts at $20 per unit per month, quoted as a flat monthly fee based on your community’s size, common areas, amenities, financial complexity, and service scope. We never price as a percentage of your budget, and we do not add a separate capital-project planning or oversight fee. Third-party costs such as contractors, engineers, and attorneys remain association expenses.

### Can CenterPoint help an HOA enforce rules consistently?
Yes. CenterPoint builds documented workflows around the association’s declaration, bylaws, rules, notices, response periods, hearings, and board decisions so similar matters follow a consistent process. Association counsel is consulted when legal advice is required.

### Can our HOA switch management companies before the contract ends?
Usually, yes, most Chicago-area management contracts allow termination with 30 to 90 days written notice, and some allow immediate termination for cause. Have your board review the termination clause, then time the notice so our managed 30-60 day transition lands at the handover date. We coordinate records, banking, vendors, and owner communication so the community never feels the seam.

### Do you manage townhome communities and single-family HOAs?
Yes. Alongside condominium associations, CenterPoint manages townhome communities and single-family homeowners associations across Chicago and the North Shore, including planned developments with private streets, shared landscaping, and amenity spaces. See our townhome management practice for the specifics of fee-simple and shared-element communities.

### Is our community too small or too large for CenterPoint?
If we cannot serve your community to that standard, we will say so in the first conversation.

### How is CenterPoint different from national HOA management firms?
One dedicated manager instead of a rotating account team, a flat fee instead of percentage-based pricing, a Chicago office that answers its own 24/7 line instead of a national call center, and monthly board-ready financials instead of quarterly boilerplate.
